Exact failed-retry logic: when runCooldown>0, canUse decrements it, then unconditionally assigns400+nextInt600 before false return. Any failed zero search also assigns positive; completed sip does too. With only the shown methods and same goal object, later eligible canUse evaluations never reach the zero/search else again after this positive assignment. sipCooldown>0 pauses even that evaluation. This is bounded source-order inference, not live starvation/reload exploit; no claim all instances never sip since first canUse can succeed and other runtime mutations/reconstruction are outside this object contract.

Movement is direct FlightMoveController wanted position; above and airborne it aims just above feeder, otherwise random nearby rise. Controller applies velocity, unused canReach helper is never called from tick, so path safety is not guaranteed.

Within Euclidean distance<2.5 and birdY>feederY it increments idleAtFlowerTime, caches feederPos and broadcasts event68. Counter does not reset simply for an out-of-range tick; interruption stop does reset. Completion strictly>55 qualifying feeder-goal updates, not56 guaranteed consecutive world ticks. Goal default requiresUpdateEveryTick=false, Mob half-phase scheduling means do not turn updates into fixed wall time. Does not reset visitation counter, require actual drained state or commit a resource-use receipt. Initial two ingredients can support multiple conceptual visits but same-object retry defect/other gates preclude a guaranteed long-run economy.

It only calls parent when adult and pollinateCooldown==0, so eligibility/flag arbitration gates retry decrement. Target is current hummingbird_pollinates tag and LOS clip; nearest algorithm is native ordered rectangular rings/restriction test, not proven shortest flight path.

Pollination tick first calls native parent tick, which adjusts tryTicks/repaths using3D center distance; override then adjusts tryTicks a second time using XZ integer-truncated AMBlockPos coordinates at targetY and strict squared<9. AMBlockPos casts doubles to int (toward zero, not floor); target from parent is blockPos.above.
